title: Stochastic burn and price-trigger lab
content:
Purpose and brief

Quick note: this is a working lab doc to prototype a stochastic approach to burn forecasting tied to pricing sensitivity and headcount gating. Aim is to produce a lightweight rulebook that product, infra, and SRE can use when demand deviates from baseline so we can 1) delay hires in controlled buckets, 2) trigger price nudges or temporary slabs, and 3) preserve SLA buffers. Not a final policy — experimental dataset for Q3 planning.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Build a stochastic burn simulator seeded from daily token demand distributions (post-PLG traffic).
- Derive a hazard curve for runway breach at 90/60/30 day horizons per commit level.
- Map hazard percentiles to three action tiers: Soft (rate plan nudge), Moderate (freeze non-critical hire buckets), Hard (price floor + burst capacity rebalancing).
- Define headcount gating windows (HC-Buckets A/B/C) with quantifiable cost avoided if triggered.

Key concepts / vocabulary
- Stochastic burn: simulate daily spend using sampled token intensity, model mix, and GPU spot price noise. Output: probability distribution of run-rate and runway days.
- Hazard curve: P(runway <= X days) for X in {30,60,90}. Used to pick trigger probability thresholds.
- Price-deceleration slope: expected % change in committed price sensitivity per 10% drop in demand over 4 weeks.
- HC-Buckets: grouped pending hires by criticality and projected cost-to-complete.

Assumptions (base case)
- ARR growth baseline: 2.5% weekly net new usage; churn steady.
- Average token mix shift toward embeddings + short chat (30% shift) if adoption of new SDKs continues.
- GPU unit cost mean = $0.85/hr (on-demand equivalent), stdev = 0.09 (captures regional spot variance).
- Model mix: 55% open-weights medium models, 30% quantized large, 15% high-quality tuned (expensive).
- Current committed reserve coverage: 4 months of planned burst capacity.

Modeling notes (how it’s built)
- Input series: daily tokens by cohort (free, trial, paid), model selection probabilities, per-token compute cost, infra spot noise (AR(1) residuals).
- Monte Carlo: 10k trajectories for 180 days horizon. Each trajectory includes a stochastic demand shock process (Poisson jump process + autoregressive trend).
- Outputs: median burn, P10/P90, hazard curve at 30/60/90 days, expected savings if HC gating triggers at each percentile.

Sample output (illustrative numbers from prototype run — 05/28/2026 seed)
- Median 90d burn: $12.1M
- P10 90d burn: $9.2M
- P90 90d burn: $15.8M
- Hazard (runway <= 60d) at current burn = 18%
- If price cut by 5% across-exchange for small customers, expected reduction in burn volatility = 7% (reduces hazard to 14%)

Headcount gating (HC-Buckets)
- Bucket A (mission-critical): infra-SRE oncall rotation hires, dedicated infra engineers for Private product. Delay cost high; avoid if hazard > 50%.
- Bucket B (high-value near-term): product and platform hires that accelerate revenue integration. Delay cost medium; freeze if hazard in (30%,50%].
- Bucket C (nice-to-have / long lead): exploratory applied-ML and growth roles. Freeze immediately if hazard > 10%.
- Quick numbers: delaying Bucket B by 12 weeks saves ~$780k in compensation + hiring overhead.

Pricing sensitivity rules (playbook)
- Soft nudge (Tier 1): at hazard 10–20% for 60d, send proactive SKU email and raise new-customer minimum slab. Expected impact: 1–3% reduction in token churn and 0.5% reduction in revenue.
- Moderate (Tier 2): hazard 20–40%, increase per-token price for non-enterprise customers by 4% and open a temporary discounted reserved plan for strategic customers to preserve committed revenue. Expected: 5–9% drop in on-demand volume, 2–3% increase in unit price realized.
- Hard (Tier 3): hazard > 40%, enable price floor (minimum unit price), move low-margin customers to metered-only or require minimal commit. Also throttle low-priority burst pools. Expected immediate burn reduction 12–22%.

Operational runbook snippets (what finance/ops do)
- Daily: publish hazard snapshot to #finance-ops and product-leads at 09:30 PT. Attach top 10 customers contributing to increased volatility.
- Weekly: run sensitivity matrix with alternate price slopes (-5%, 0%, +5%, +10%) and HC gating simulation. Post results to Confluence page (link above).
- Trigger protocol: if hazard crosses a boundary and stays for 3 business days, convene a triage huddle (finance, sales lead, product, infra). Fresh decision within 48hrs.

Mini example calculation (how a trigger saves cash)
- Scenario: hazard moves to 35% -> Tier 2 trigger.
- Projected 90d burn (median) without action: $13.4M. With Tier2 pricing + HC freeze: median burn = $11.6M. Delta saved = $1.8M.
- Cost of delaying Bucket B hires (3 roles) = $780k -> net avoided cash outflow for 90d window = $1.02M.

Open questions / unknowns
- Elasticity at small-customer slab boundaries is noisy; need real A/B tests for price slope.
- Impact of model-quantization adoption on unit economics not fully modeled; runs assume static model mix.
- Sales churn risk from mid-tier price changes (Tier 2) — need sales-signed whitelist and exceptions list.

Next steps / immediate asks
- Engineering: wire daily token-by-cohort export to /data/finance/usage-daily.csv (see FIN-3421).
- Product: propose initial Tier2 price uplift test for a 30-day window targeting low-commit accounts (sample size ~150 customers).
- SRE: produce a burst-pool tagging map by 06/09 so we can quantify savings from temporary throttles.
- Finance: iterate the Monte Carlo with two additional scenarios: rapid-adoption (double weekly growth) and rapid-decay (monthly -20%).

Notes / references
- Prototype notebook: git pr #88 (linked above).
- Slack threads: #finance-ops pinned messages (see timestamp link).
- Reference frame: conservatively assume last hire offers can be paused within 10 business days; hiring freeze cost = full comp loss of role until restart.

Metadata / provenance
- Built from Q1 and Q2 usage traces + region spot price sampling. Seed date for current model: 2026-05-28.
- Owner: Asha Patel (finance) — use this doc to coordinate cross-team experiments.
